summary: Under a CEMAC Additional Act, citizens of CEMAC member states may travel without a visa and stay in any other member state for up to 90 days. The Congolese embassy in Washington says no Congolese visa is issued at any port of entry and applications must be made before departure, and the UK, Canadian and German governments say their citizens need a visa obtained before travel; no official source we could read states the rule for most other nationalities.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based; major hotels and stores generally accept major credit cards, as well as euros and US dollars (confirm when booking), but outside these establishments in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire credit cards are rarely accepted.

safety.text: The UK government reports opportunistic crime such as pickpocketing, particularly in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, says criminals may target foreigners, and advises extra precautions against vehicle crime, especially outside urban centres and anywhere in the Pool Region and Mouyondzi District. It says live conflict has not been reported in the Pool Region since a 2017 ceasefire, but violent clashes could arise again with little or no notice. It advises against all travel to within 50 km of the border with the Central African Republic in Likouala Region, against walking in the streets after dark, and to always carry a colour copy of your passport including your visa entry stamp, as police may ask for ID.

tips.text: The UK government's factfile says Congo is often called Congo-Brazzaville to distinguish it from its neighbour, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (sometimes called Congo-Kinshasa).
The UK government says you must have certificates proving yellow fever and polio vaccination to pass border control.

The UK government says police may ask you for ID and to always carry a colour copy of your passport, including your visa entry stamp; the Government of Canada says you may be detained by police if you are unable to produce acceptable identification.
The Government of Canada says the economy is primarily cash-based and that, outside major hotels and stores in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, credit cards are rarely accepted.

The Government of Canada says it is illegal to photograph government buildings, military installations, border crossings and transportation infrastructure, including ports, train stations and airports, and advises seeking permission before taking photos of official buildings or individuals.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for the Republic of the Congo?
faq.answer: Under a CEMAC Additional Act, citizens of CEMAC member states may travel without a visa for stays of up to 90 days, and under a Congo–Rwanda agreement Rwandan ordinary-passport holders get a free visa on entry. The Congolese embassy in Washington says visa applications must be submitted before departure, and the UK, Canadian and German governments say their citizens need a visa obtained before travel. No official source we could read states the rule for most other nationalities, and none describes an electronic visa.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Congo-Brazzaville?
faq.answer: Under a Congo–Rwanda agreement, Rwandan ordinary-passport holders get a free visa on entry, valid for up to 90 days. The Congolese embassy in Washington says no Congolese visa is issued at any port of entry, and Canada's and Germany's travel advice say their citizens cannot get a visa on arrival.

faq.question: Is this the same country as the DRC?
faq.answer: No. The UK government's factfile says Congo is often called Congo-Brazzaville to distinguish it from its neighbour, the Democratic Republic of the Congo (sometimes called Congo-Kinshasa), and lists the Democratic Republic of the Congo among the countries it shares land boundaries with; its travel advice describes the river border crossing between Brazzaville and Kinshasa.

faq.question: Is yellow fever vaccination required for the Republic of the Congo?
faq.answer: Yes. The UK government says that to pass border control you must have certificates proving yellow fever vaccination and polio vaccination.

faq.question: Is the Republic of the Congo safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK government advises against all travel to within 50 km of the border with the Central African Republic in Likouala Region, and says violent clashes could arise again with little or no notice in the Pool Region. It reports opportunistic crime such as pickpocketing, particularly in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire, and advises avoiding walking in the streets after dark.
